thread:
fionn-murphy: Hi payroll team — my Aug 31 paystub seems to have both Irish PAYE/PRSI/USC and UK PAYE taxes deducted on the same pay run. Net is way lower than I expected. Anyone can help? :worried:
ireland-payroll: Sorry @fionn-murphy. Can you paste the paystub lines (redact acct) or DM a screenshot?
fionn-murphy: Pasting redacted lines (monthly salary pro-rated):
```
Period: 2026-08-16 to 2026-08-31
Gross: 3,800.00 EUR
Irish PAYE: -560.00 EUR
PRSI: -150.00 EUR
USC: -85.00 EUR
UK PAYE: -420.00 GBP
Employee pension: -19.00 GBP
Net paid: x,xxx.xx
```
uk-payroll: Thanks. Looks like two payroll rows were exported for the Aug biweekly run: an Ireland resident row and a UK resident row for the same employee. That can happen when a mid-month relocation isn't gated properly.
sophie-hr: Fionn submitted relocation to the Dublin office on 2026-08-18; HR updated Workday on 2026-08-19. I see the Ireland termination notice was entered but the effective termination date on the UK payroll feed wasn't set before the August 16 payroll close.
payroll-bot: Ticket created: PR-50177 "Dual Ireland/UK withholding on fionn-murphy Aug 2026". Assigned to GlobalPay. ETA provider ack 48h.
tax-advisor: Quick tax note: Residency mid-month can create overlapping statutory obligations. Usually we determine tax residency by effective date and correct payroll reporting; refunds/reclaims may be needed if both jurisdictions were reported. Keep all stubs for year-end P60/P45 and Irish P60 equivalents.
finance-ops: @ireland-payroll please estimate the shortfall in EUR so we can approve a one-time net relief if needed.
ireland-payroll: Estimated net shortfall ~670 EUR after FX. Operational plan: 1) request GlobalPay to reverse the duplicate UK PAYE deductions for the Irish resident days, 2) apply an adjustment line in Sep payroll to credit the net shortfall (labeled "relocation reimbursement"), 3) coordinate with UK team to confirm whether ER/EE NI was reported and whether employer NI reclaim needed.
uk-payroll: Confirming: if the UK export included NI or PAYE submission, HMRC may already have a record. We'll need to submit an amendment and/or reclaim. UK reporting changes can require a P46C or manual adjustment depending on timing.
fionn-murphy: Will this affect my year-end statements? I'm worried about both a UK P60 and Irish equivalent with conflicting earnings.
tax-advisor: It will affect year-end reporting for both jurisdictions and we will provide a reconciliation pack for your tax advisor. Typically one jurisdiction will get amended reporting (W-2c/P60c style) and the other will show corrected totals. We'll handle coordination and provide documentation for tax filings.
sophie-hr: I'll escalate the relocation cutover checklist and add a mandatory "payroll termination confirmed" step before creating the new resident export for mid-month moves.
payroll-bot: PR-50177 updated: finance approval requested for one-time net make-whole up to 700 EUR.
finance-ops: Approved provisional one-time net reimbursement up to 700 EUR pending provider confirmation. Label it "relocation shortfall" and mark non-recurring.
ireland-payroll: Noted. We will also check equity/payment components — I see Fionn had a discretionary allowance paid Aug 20; we'll audit that line in case it was taxed twice.
uk-payroll: Also note: pension and student loan code could get misapplied if two starter records exist. We'll freeze any ongoing UK deductions until we confirm the reversal.
fionn-murphy: Appreciate it. Please confirm when the net adjustment will hit my Sep payroll if the provider delays. I may need funds earlier.
ireland-payroll: If GlobalPay delays beyond Sep 5, finance approved an emergency hardship payment as a cash advance; we'll post it as a recoverable relocation reimbursement and reconcile later.
payroll-bot: PR-50177 updated: GlobalPay acknowledged, awaiting reversal docs.
ireland-payroll: Closing loop for now — actions: provider reversal request submitted; Sep payroll adjustment planned; hardship payment available if provider takes >2 weeks. We'll attach corrected paystub and provider ticket number when available. Thanks for flagging, @fionn-murphy.
